text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- The consortium led by Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) was named as the government's consultant for the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell was named as runner up.
LIETUVOS RYTAS

- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will meet in Vilnius with foreign ministers from Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia as well as Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas and Parliamentary Chairman Vytautas Landsbergis on July 13.
- Vilniaus Bank assets reached 1.012 billion litas at the end of May, an increase of 2.2 times from May 1996.

- The board of Lithuania's stock exchange has placed Naftotiekis shares on its current list from July 7. Naftotiekis' emission of 6.113 million shares has a total nominal value of 61.129 million litas.
- Mazheikiu Nafta refined 2.76 million tonnes of oil in the first half of 1997, 1.8 times more than in the same period in 1996.
VERSLO ZINIOS
- Experts Lithuanian Telecom is worth around 1.5 billion litas.

- Lithuanian brokerage house Suprema does not rule out the possibility of distributing the remainder of Vilniaus Vingis' issue of 2.764 million ordinary shares, which have an issue price of 5.8 litas.

- GDP increased by 2.4 percent in the first quarter compared to the same period last year. GDP for the first quarter was 8.154 billion litas. GDP per capita in the first quarter was 2,200 litas, compared to 1,742 litas in the same period last year.
RESPUBLIKA
- Parliament set December 21 as the date for presidential elections.

- President Algirdas Brazauskas will go to Paris and Madrid from July 7-10. In Paris he will meet with French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, and in Madrid he will be at the NATO summit.
- Parliament removed May 1, the international day of workers, from Lithuania's list of holidays.

- Lithuania received more foreign investment in 1996 than Estonia or Latvia. Lithunia attracted $220 million in foreign investment, Estonia $138 million and Latvia $100 million last year. Estonia led the way in per capita investment.
LIETUVOS AIDAS

- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said the government had completed a programme of agricultural credits for enterprises to pay for new equipment. He warned that the issuing of credits will be governed by tight rules.
-- Burton Frierson, Vilnius newsroom +370 2 22 35 17
